output.reason: On its own, the cited "- application" line [ev-c8bbef5b1d06] is just one item in a list. The section around it [ev-b07a4021f30c] gives it a concrete meaning: Loki 3.0 now adds a `service_name` label to all ingested logs by default. It takes the value from the first label it finds in a fixed order: service_name, service, app, application, and so on [ev-92063a2a5bac, ev-2690c7915f58, ev-61d6d2b50a95]. If none is present, it uses `unknown_service`. Operators can change or disable this through `discover_service_name` in limits_config, and logs that already have a `service_name` label are left alone. So the subject is the `application` label as a source in the new default service_name discovery, the change is new default behaviour, and the consequence is that matching logs get a `service_name` label taken from that label. Exposure is logs that have an `application` label but none of the labels earlier in the list, under the default `discover_service_name` setting.
